confirmed.title: Select All ignores the kind tab: it selects every flow in the org, including the hidden kinds
confirmed.scenario: Flows view, Delete mode, org with 200 flows of which 3 are scheduled. Click the '📅 Scheduled' tab (list shows 3 rows), click Select All. Every version of all 200 flows is added to selectedIds; only the summary line count hints at it, the list shows 3 ticked rows. Delete then removes flows of kinds that are not on screen. Select All does honour the search box, so the user expects it to honour the tab as well.
confirmed.why: The claim survives. In the frozen copy, popup.js:1844-1853 (the selectAllBtn handler) loops over every entry of flowGroups and skips only on the search box (line 1847); it never reads _flowTypeFilter. The kind tabs are new in this range (popup.js:1440-1472, click handler at 2459, markup at popup.html:161-166) and renderFlowList hides rows by kind at popup.js:1498 and 1509 (kindHit). So with the Scheduled tab on and the search box empty, Select All adds every version of every flow in the org to selectedIds while the list shows only the scheduled trees. No guard downstream narrows it: onDeleteClick (popup.js:1885-1888) builds its set as allFlows.filter(f => selectedIds.has(f.Id)), with no kind check. The tab click (2459) does not clear or trim selectedIds either. The only hints are the summary line (updateSelectionSummary, 3394-3408: "N versions selected across 200 flows") and whatever the delete confirmation modals show (the active-flow warning at 1890-1895 fires only if some selected version is active). I did not read the later confirm steps in onDeleteClick, so the user may get one more count before the delete, but the selection itself is wrong and off screen. One nuance to the scenario: the list shows a whole tree when any flow in it is of the picked kind (1507-1509), so the visible set can include subflows of other kinds; the fix should match that or be stricter.
confirmed.fix: In the selectAllBtn handler (popup.js:1844), apply the same kind test renderFlowList uses. Smallest form: build trigMap as line 1492 does, iterate sftkFlowListRows(flowGroups) instead of Object.entries(flowGroups), and skip a row when _flowTypeFilter !== 'all' && sftkFlowKindTab(sftkFlowKindOfRow(row, trigMap)) !== _flowTypeFilter (keeping the existing search skip on row.labels/row.apiName), then add row.versions ids. This selects only flows of the picked kind; subflows of another kind shown inside a visible tree stay unticked, which is the safe side for a delete.

confirmed.title: Update under a PII policy now sends null person fields on business accounts, which is likely to fail every such row
confirmed.scenario: Both orgs have Person Accounts on. The policy covers Account person fields (FirstName, LastName, PersonEmail, PersonMobilePhone - the suggestion window pre-ticks name parts, e-mails and phones). The user selects changed business accounts for 'update (source wins)'. The source holds those fields empty on a business account, so the payload now carries FirstName: null, LastName: null, PersonEmail: null. Before this change the fields were skipped and the update went through. Salesforce refuses person-account fields named on a business account (INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE, 'Business Account may not use Person Account field'), so each business-account row would fail. Only the person-account Name is guarded, and nothing checks IsPersonAccount before the empty write. Not confirmed against an org: it rests on Salesforce treating an explicit null the same as a value here.
confirmed.why:
Not refuted in code; the one open point is Salesforce's own behaviour, which I could not test (no org may be touched).

**What the code does** (`C:/Users/yonas/AppData/Local/Temp/sftk-qa-84d029b/studio-reconcile.js`, `reconcileOverwrite`):
- Lines 4872-4877: when the source value is null and `sftkRecPiiEmptyWrites(piiActive, piiRules, sf)` is true, the payload gets `p[tf] = null`. The diff f4278a0..84d029b shows this replaced a plain `if (v == null) continue;`, so it is a behaviour change.
- Lines 4522-4524: `sftkRecPiiEmptyWrites` checks only that the policy is active, the field is not `RecordTypeId`, and the field has a rule. It never looks at the record.
- Line 4867: the only use of `IsPersonAccount` in the loop is the `Name` skip for person accounts. Line 4733 selects the flag for that purpose alone.
- Lines 4693-4705: the target-side filter drops fields that are missing or read-only in the target describe. With Person Accounts on in the target, `FirstName`, `LastName`, `PersonEmail` and `PersonMobilePhone` are present and updateable on Account, so they stay in `srcFields` for every row.
- Lines 4900-4935: nothing after the loop strips nulls or person fields from the payload.

So a business-account row under a policy covering person fields is sent with those fields as explicit nulls, where before they were omitted.

**The part I could not confirm:** whether Salesforce rejects an explicit null on a person field of a business account. My recollection is that it does (INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE, "Business Account may not use Person Account field", as seen with Data Loader's "Insert Null Values" on mixed Account files), but this is from memory, not from an org or the docs. If Salesforce accepts the null, the claim falls.
confirmed.fix:
In the `v == null` branch at studio-reconcile.js:4872-4877, skip the empty write when the source row is a business account and the field is a person-only field. `IsPersonAccount` is already selected (line 4733) and `descByLower` is in scope. For example:

`const personOnly = objType === 'Account' && sr.IsPersonAccount === false && (/^Person/i.test(sf) || /__pc$/i.test(sf) || ['firstname','lastname','salutation','middlename','suffix'].includes(sf.toLowerCase()));`
`if (!personOnly && sftkRecPiiEmptyWrites(piiActive, piiRules, sf)) { ... }`

A business account cannot hold these fields in the target either, so skipping loses no masking.

confirmed.title: Scan warning states as fact that written records cannot be found and will be duplicated, for any filter that merely names a disguised field
confirmed.scenario: The policy fabricates Lead.Email (or LastName) and the record filter is 'Email != null' (or 'LastName != null AND Status = ...'). The fabricated value is still non-empty, so the same filter on the target finds every record already written and nothing is listed under Insert again. The scan still adds the line on every scan, before any bucket is computed: 'A record this deployment already wrote to the target is held there under its fabricated value, so the filter cannot find it: it is listed under Insert again, and deploying it again creates a duplicate.' sftkScanPiiBlind only tests that the field name appears outside quotes; it does not look at the operator or at whether anything is actually left over. The match-key variant is gated on leftovers in both orgs (sftkScanPiiBlindKeysMatter); the filter variant is not gated at all.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives. In C:/Users/yonas/AppData/Local/Temp/sftk-qa-84d029b/studio-scan.js:

- Line 721-736 (sftkScanPiiBlind): a field goes into out.filter if its name appears anywhere outside quotes in the filter (regex at line 734). It does not look at the operator or the compared value. Any truthy policy rule counts (line 727), whatever its strategy.
- Line 1324-1329: the filter line is pushed to memWarnings unconditionally, before any bucket exists: `const line = sftkScanPiiBlindLine(objType, { keys: [], filter: _piiBlind.filter }); if (line) memWarnings.push(line);`. Nothing later removes it.
- Line 745 (sftkScanPiiBlindLine): with a non-empty filter list the text is categorical: "A record this deployment already wrote to the target is held there under its fabricated value, so the filter cannot find it: it is listed under Insert again, and deploying it again creates a duplicate."
- Line 802 and 1069: the same `where` (node.where) is run against both orgs, so with `Email != null` and a fabricating strategy (e.g. { strategy: 'pattern', pattern: 'email-person' }) the fabricated, non-empty target value satisfies the filter. The target rows are read and paired by an undisguised match key or by match memory, and nothing is listed under Insert. The sentence is then false on every scan.
- Line 1836: the match-key variant is gated by sftkScanPiiBlindKeysMatter (leftovers on both sides, line 737-739). The filter variant has no such gate.
- test/pii-selected-1121.test.mjs:81-109 only covers the name detection and the wording; no test ties the filter line to the buckets.

The live case that motivated it (LastName LIKE 'SFTK PII%') is a value comparison, where the sentence is true. For null checks, or when the filter has an unrelated clause plus a null check on the disguised field, it states a duplicate risk that does not exist. I found no guard, caller or Salesforce behaviour that prevents this.
confirmed.fix: Gate the filter variant on the buckets, as the key variant already is. At line 1327 keep only the computation of _piiBlind and drop the push. At line 1836 add: if _piiBlind.filter.length && missingInTarget.length > 0, push sftkScanPiiBlindLine(objType, { keys: [], filter: _piiBlind.filter }). In sftkScanPiiBlindLine (line 745) soften the filter wording from "so the filter cannot find it: it is listed under Insert again" to conditional wording, e.g. "If records listed under Insert are ones this deployment already wrote, the filter may not find them in the target under their fabricated value, and deploying them again creates duplicates." Optionally, in sftkScanPiiBlind skip a field whose only uses in the filter are `= null` / `!= null` when its rule's strategy is not 'null'.

confirmed.title: Disguise button stays enabled when a run starts, so the policy can be changed and saved under a live run
confirmed.scenario: Tick inserts on the root and updates on a child, press Deploy and confirm. runReconcile sets window._sftkRunActive and locks only dsRecRunBtn and dsRecProbeBtn (_recRunBtnsLock). #dsDepPiiSel is disabled for a run only inside _depSummary, which is not called when the run starts, so the button stays live until some repaint happens. Press it, tick fields, Apply. bldPiiApplyRules mutates the same profile object the run holds, and every later leg reads profile.piiPolicy live (engine legs are sent the profile at leg time; reconcileOverwrite builds piiRules at call time). The result is one run whose earlier legs wrote raw values and whose later legs wrote disguised ones, and whose updates now write empties into covered fields, none of which the run's confirmation mentioned. _depPiiSuggest then saves the profile and calls renderDeploy() mid-run. Neither the click handler nor _depPiiSuggest checks _sftkRunActive.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives. In the frozen copy:

- studio-reconcile.js:3042-3047 — at run start runReconcile calls _recRunBtnsLock(true) and sets window._sftkRunActive = true. _recRunBtnsLock (2548-2550) touches only 'dsRecRunBtn' and 'dsRecProbeBtn'. Nothing there repaints the Deploy page or calls _depSummary.
- studio-deploy.js:2764 — `piiBtn.disabled = !sc.total || !!window._sftkRunActive || !!p.ephemeral;` is the only place #dsDepPiiSel is disabled for a run, and it runs only inside _depSummary (called from renderDeploy :740, a tick repaint :2054, :2172). So the author meant the button to be off during a run, but it stays enabled until some unrelated repaint happens.
- studio-deploy.js:772-776 — the click handler checks only sc.total (the selection is still ticked during the run; _recSel is reset only at the end, studio-reconcile.js:4028). No _sftkRunActive check.
- studio-deploy.js:1373-1388 — _depPiiSuggest checks only p.ephemeral, opens bldOpenPiiSuggestModal (studio-builder.js:2662, no run check), then storageSaveProfiles() and renderDeploy() mid-run.
- The run holds the same object: studio-deploy.js:2578/2587 pass p itself to runReconcile. Each leg re-reads it at leg time: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(profile)) at studio-reconcile.js:3325, 3457, 3730, 3775; profile?.piiPolicy at 3588 (relink) and 3784; reconcileOverwrite builds piiRules from profile.piiPolicy at call time (4572-4579) and writes null into covered fields (4875). The confirmation read piiPolicy once before the run (206, 241).

So with root inserts plus child updates/overwrites ticked, pressing Disguise + Apply after the first leg changes what later legs write (disguised inserts, emptied covered fields on updates, relink skipped at 3591), none of it in the confirmation the user accepted. I found no overlay, modal or guard that blocks the button during a run.
confirmed.fix: Guard the entry point rather than only the button paint: at the top of _depPiiSuggest (studio-deploy.js:1373) add `if (window._sftkRunActive) return showToast('A run is in progress — change the disguise policy when it has finished.', 'info', 5000);` (covers both #dsDepPiiSel and #dsDepPiiAll). Optionally also add 'dsDepPiiSel' to the id list in _recRunBtnsLock (studio-reconcile.js:2549) so the button greys out at run start; on unlock _depSummary re-evaluates it at the next repaint.

confirmed.title: Never-set rule shows "Ignore small differences" on and a live result computed with it, but Apply saves nothing — the scan and run match exactly
confirmed.scenario: Open Pick Records on a node that has no node.matching (any new object, e.g. Account). The switch "Ignore small differences" is checked and the live result is computed with all five normalizations (runMatchLive uses matchNormalize), e.g. source "ACME Ltd " vs target "acme ltd" reads "1 are already in the target — a run updates them". Tick some records and press Apply without touching the rule. The Apply handler only writes node.recordIds; persistMatching() runs only on a rule change, so node.matching stays undefined. studio-scan.js then builds the key as { strategy:'field', fields:[derived.matchField], normalize:{} } — exact match — so the same record is reported missing and a run creates a duplicate. CHANGELOG line 28 says the switch "is on for a rule that was never set"; the saved deployment does not keep it. Before the change the unsaved default was all-off, which equalled what the engine did.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard. All paths are in C:/Users/yonas/AppData/Local/Temp/sftk-qa-84d029b.

- **Default is session-only.** studio-builder-modals.js:821 (added in this range, per the diff) sets `matchNormalize` to all five true when `!node.matching`. It never touches the node.
- **The UI shows it and computes with it.** The fold is open by default for an unconfigured node (line 1285: `cfgd ? '' : 'open'`), so line 1757 runs `runMatchLive()` on open. Line 1702 builds a temp node with `normalize: { ...matchNormalize }` and passes `m.normalize` to `sftkAnalyzeMatchKey` (line 1716). The live sentence is therefore computed with the forgiving key.
- **Apply does not save it.** `persistMatching()` (line 878) is called only from change handlers: `matchCfgChanged` (1429), the norm checkboxes (1486), the upsert toggle (1499) and the Test button (1507). The `dsRecSave` handler (1927-1937) writes only `node.recordIds` and calls `commitEditingProfile()`. Its comment "matching edits were applied to the node live" is true only for edits, not for the unsaved default.
- **The engine then matches exactly.** studio-scan.js:776-780: with `node.matching` undefined, `hasMatchingCfg` is false and the key is `{ strategy: 'field', fields: [derived.matchField], normalize: {} }`. sftk-matching.js:33-53 (`sftkNormalizeValue`) does nothing for an empty normalize, so "ACME Ltd " and "acme ltd" produce different keys. `sftkMatchingFromNode` (sftk-matching.js:153-157) also returns `normalize: {}` for a legacy node.
- **The on-screen and changelog sentence is not kept.** CHANGELOG.md:28 says the switch "is on for a rule that was never set". After an untouched Apply the saved deployment has no such setting.

It is a regression: before line 821 the unsaved default was all-off, which equalled the engine's behaviour.

I did not trace the writer in background.js; the scan mismatch alone makes the live sentence false.
confirmed.fix:
In the `dsRecSave` click handler (studio-builder-modals.js:1927), before `closeModal()`, add `if (!node.matching) persistMatching();` so the rule shown on screen, with the forgiving normalize, is what gets saved.

One caveat: this sets `hasMatchingCfg` true for the node, which skips the unconfigured-key fallback at studio-scan.js:909 for objects with no usable Name. If that matters, guard the persist to nodes where the Matching fold was rendered with a real key field. The alternative is to drop line 821 and turn the five options on at the first rule change instead.

confirmed.title: Stale live result painted for a rule that is no longer on screen: the cache-hit path does not advance matchLiveSeq
confirmed.scenario: Rule A has been checked (matchLive.sig = A). Untick "Ignore small differences" (or flip the tiered Yes/No, or change a field): rule B starts with seq = ++matchLiveSeq, a 350 ms wait and then queries of both orgs. Before B's answer lands, tick the switch back (rule A again). runMatchLive hits the cache for A, paints A and returns WITHOUT bumping matchLiveSeq or clearing the timer. B's run then passes both `seq !== matchLiveSeq` checks, sets matchLive = B and paint() succeeds because it only compares matchLive.sig with its own sig. The panel now shows B's counts (and possibly B's "Use it" offer) under rule A's sentence, and stays that way until the next re-render.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives. C:/Users/yonas/AppData/Local/Temp/sftk-qa-84d029b/studio-builder-modals.js:
- Line 843: `let matchLive = null, matchLiveSeq = 0, matchLiveTimer = null;` is modal-scope. It is only written at 1710, 1712-1713 and 1726. Nothing else resets it: matchCfgChanged (1428-1442) only re-renders and re-wires, which calls runMatchLive again at 1757.
- Line 1709: `if (matchLive && matchLive.sig === sig) { el0.innerHTML = matchLive.html; wireLive(); return; }` returns before `const seq = ++matchLiveSeq;` (1710) and before `clearTimeout(matchLiveTimer)` (1712). A cache hit therefore does not invalidate a run in flight.
- While rule B is in its 350 ms wait or its queries, matchLive still holds A (it is only replaced at 1726), so switching back to A does hit the cache.
- B's run then passes `if (seq !== matchLiveSeq) return;` at 1714 and 1718, and sets `matchLive = { sig, ... }` with B's sig at 1726.
- paint() at 1727 checks only `matchLive.sig === sig`, B against B, and looks up `eid('dsMatchLive')` fresh, so it writes B's result into the re-rendered panel that shows rule A's sentence.
- If B's tone is bad or warn, the loop at 1734-1740 also runs to the end and paints a "Use it" offer computed for B. wireLive (1742-1752) applies matchLive.best from it.
I found no guard: nothing compares the painted sig with the rule currently on screen. The wrong result stays until the next re-render, where the sig mismatch triggers a fresh check of A.
confirmed.fix: In runMatchLive, make the cache-hit path at line 1709 invalidate any run in flight and keep the cached offer: `if (matchLive && matchLive.sig === sig) { ++matchLiveSeq; clearTimeout(matchLiveTimer); el0.innerHTML = matchLive.html + (matchLive.reco || ''); wireLive(); return; }`. Simplest form: move `const seq = ++matchLiveSeq; clearTimeout(matchLiveTimer);` above the cache check. Do the same bump on the "Pick a target org" early return at 1705.

confirmed.title: With the default "match by the first field alone: Yes", the examples come from exact full-key equality and can contradict the counts beside them
confirmed.scenario: Sentence of two fields, e.g. Name and Email; adding the second field sets matchTiered = true. Source holds Acme / a@acme.com, target holds Acme / (no email), and there is at least one genuinely new source record. The counts come from sftkTieredPreview (the scan's pairing), which pairs Acme by Name alone and counts it under "already in the target". The examples come from bldMatchExamples, which compares the full composite keys in keyCounts: "acme·a@acme.com" has no exact target key, so it becomes onlySrc and is printed under "are not in the target yet — a run creates them — for example “acme · a@acme.com”". The row "already in the target" can likewise have no example, and the clash example and its "N in the source, N in the target" are counted by exact key, not by the tiered groups.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives. Nothing between the counts and the examples reconciles the two pairings when the rule is tiered.

- **Counts use the scan's tiered pairing.** `studio-builder-modals.js:2373-2375` sets `out.cross` from `sftkTieredPreview(out.src.parts, out.tgt.parts)` when `tiered` is true. `sftkTieredScore` (`sftk-matching.js:569-580`) skips a component that is empty on either side, so source `['acme','a@acme.com']` against target `['acme','']` scores 1 and is paired. It is counted in `matchedUnique`.
- **Examples use exact full-key equality.** `studio-builder-modals.js:1723` always calls `bldMatchExamples(res.src, res.tgt, ...)`, with no check of `m.tiered` or `res.cross.tiered`. `keyCounts` comes from `sftkKeyCountsFromRecords` → `sftkMatchKey` (`sftk-matching.js:126-134`), which joins all parts. The source key is `acme\x01a@acme.com` and the target key is `acme\x01`. At `studio-builder-modals.js:2222-2224`, `tk.get(k)` is 0, so `out.onlySrc` becomes "acme · a@acme.com".
- **The only guard is the row count.** `bldMatchLiveHtml` (line 2270) prints the example when `r.ex && r.n`. With one genuinely new source record, `unmatched` is at least 1, so the "are not in the target yet — a run creates them" row prints. If Acme comes earlier in the source read than the new record, the row shows "for example “acme · a@acme.com”", a record the same panel counts as already in the target.
- **The other two rows are affected the same way.** The "already in the target" row has n=1 but no example, because `out.both` needs an exact key on both sides. The clash example and its "N in the source, N in the target" are also by exact key, not by the tiered groups.
- **The tiered path is the default for a multi-field sentence.** Line 1467 sets `matchTiered = true` when the sentence becomes composite, and line 1702 passes `tiered: true` into the check.
confirmed.fix:
Take the examples from the same pairing as the counts when the rule is tiered.

- In `sftkTieredPreview` (`sftk-matching.js:681`), also return example keys from the pairing it already ran: `exBoth: r.pairs[0]?.[0]`, `exOnlySrc: r.inserts[0]?.[0]`, and for the first entry of `r.groups` its anchor with `srcs.length` and `tgts.length`.
- In `runMatchLive` (`studio-builder-modals.js:1723`), when `res.cross && res.cross.tiered`, build `ex` from those values through the same label function instead of calling `bldMatchExamples`.

One-line stopgap: `ex: (res.cross && res.cross.tiered) ? {} : bldMatchExamples(...)`. A tiered rule then shows no examples rather than contradictory ones.

confirmed.title: One-sided list says "none in <other org>" and "the other org has no record of the name" when the other org's copy is paired from match memory
confirmed.scenario: Source holds three Accounts named "Acme" (S1, S2, S3); the target holds one (T1). On Needs a decision the user answers only S1 = "the same record as #1", presses Apply this one, and reads both orgs again. The scan takes S1 and T1 out of key matching (memPairedSrc / memPairedTgt), so the key "Acme" counts 2 in source and 0 in target and is classed insertAll: S2 and S3 go to missingInTarget with dupKey. sftkDepOneSidedDups groups them and the tab now reads "1 name that only one org holds, more than once. There is nothing to decide here: the other org has no record of the name" and "2 copies in SRC, none in TGT - a run creates all 2 there". The target does hold "Acme" (T1, listed under Synced or Changed), and a run that follows the sentence creates two more Acme records beside it. The mirror case (one source record, three in the target, one paired from memory) prints "none in <source>" for the two left over.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard. Traced by reading the frozen copy, nothing was run.

- studio-scan.js:1336-1350 puts a memory-paired S1 and T1 into memPairedSrc / memPairedTgt, and 1390 / 1397 (and the tiered path at 1382) drop them before the key groups are built.
- With S1 and T1 gone, "Acme" counts 2 in source and 0 in target. sftk-matching.js:459-460 classes that as 'insertAll', studio-scan.js:1408 pushes S2 and S3 to _twinsNew, and 1518 files them in missingInTarget with dupKey.
- studio-deploy.js:1544-1557 (sftkDepOneSidedDups) groups only by key over missingInTarget / onlyInTarget. It skips forcedNew rows but never looks at the memory-paired, changed or identical rows, so it cannot know the target holds T1 under the same name.
- studio-deploy.js:1569 and 1579 then print "none in <target>" and "the other org has no record of the name" unconditionally.
- The partial answer is reachable: the "Apply this one" handler at studio-deploy.js:2141-2151 saves only rows where the pick differs from memory (2145). Its one guard, ambTwice at 2144, is named for double picks; I did not open it or ambSave, so that neither demands an answer for every source row is inferred from 2145.

The mirror case goes through 'extraAll' (1409, 1520) and line 1570 the same way. The run behaviour itself (creating S2 and S3) is consistent with the scan; the defect is the two on-screen sentences, which are false in this state.
confirmed.fix: Smallest change is wording, in studio-deploy.js _depOneSidedHtml, so the sentences stay true when a same-named record is already paired: - 1569: "N copies in HERE, none left unpaired in THERE — a run creates all N there." - 1570: the same "none left unpaired in THERE" for the target-side line. - 1579: "There is nothing to decide here: the other org has no unpaired record of the name." A fuller fix would have line 1944 pass sftkDepOneSidedDups the set of key labels found in s.changed and s.identical (which is where memory-paired rows land), and have the row for those names say "1 already paired in THERE" instead.

confirmed.title: A deploy that was submitted but not followed to its end is shown as refused, with no undo, in the XML editor and the ✂/⇄ edit paths
confirmed.scenario: Edit XML on a layout or Lightning page (or any other kind), Deploy, confirm. While the background polls the deploy job, the session expires, four status polls fail, or the job runs past 100 seconds. sfMetadataDeploy throws sftkDeploySubmittedError and the handler answers { error, submitted: true, jobId }. The fix commit passes submitted through the write() return, but only the delete path (7638/7641) and the code-edit path (9732/9735) act on it. In _xmlEditorDeploy wr.accepted is false, so the editor prints 'Salesforce refused the deploy — nothing was changed' and History records 'nothing was accepted by Salesforce, so there is nothing to undo'. Salesforce may still apply the deploy, and the entry then has no undo step; only the restore point remains. The same half-applied fix is in the ✂/⇄ metadata edit (finally at 7909), the search-layout edit (finally at ~7297) and restoreSnapshot (10745). background.js 5113-5114 says History never records 'nothing to undo' for such a deploy.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives. In C:/Users/yonas/AppData/Local/Temp/sftk-qa-84d029b:

- background.js 5173/5189/5193/5197/5203/5217: a real (non-check) deploy whose end is not seen throws sftkDeploySubmittedError; background.js 3831 answers { error, submitted: true, jobId }. The comment at 5113-5114 promises "History never records 'nothing to undo' for it".
- field-cleaner.js 9511: _xmlEditorDeploy's write() returns { error, submitted: true, jobId }. sftk-write.js 30-53 leaves accepted = false for any reply carrying an error, so wr.accepted is false and wr.raw.submitted is true.
- field-cleaner.js 9525-9528: there is no test of wr.raw.submitted; the code falls to 9527 and prints "Salesforce refused the deploy — nothing was changed" (the background's "MAY STILL FINISH" text appears only inside the quoted "Its words" span, contradicting the headline), and returns 'refused'.
- field-cleaner.js 9530-9537: the finally keys undo on wr.accepted only, so History records { none: 'nothing was accepted by Salesforce, so there is nothing to undo' } while the job can still be applied by Salesforce.
- Same pattern in the metadata edit: 7872 passes submitted through, 7907 throws "Salesforce refused ... Nothing was changed", and the finally at 7909 keys on wr.accepted only. The same pass-through without a consumer is at 7278, 7350, 10746, 10777.
- Only two paths consume the flag: 7638/7641 (delete) and 9732/9735 (code edit), both with `wr.accepted || (wr.raw && wr.raw.submitted)`.

confirmed.title: A validation rule whose switch-off PATCH timed out is not treated as 'maybe off': never switched back, not remembered, no leftover card
confirmed.scenario: Deploy with the rule pause ticked on an org's own (not packaged) validation rule. The Tooling PATCH that sets active=false gets no answer in time (background.js throws 'Request timed out after 30 s', or the connection drops after the request was sent) while Salesforce still applies it. The result is not accepted, so sftkVrPauseMaybeOff reaches its last line, which keeps only PACKAGED rules whose text says 'was submitted / may still finish'. The rule is left out of `touched`: it is not written to the paused-rules memory, gets no undo step, and is not in the list sftkVrPauseOn switches back on when the run refuses to start (r.failed is non-empty). verifyAll also re-reads only accepted ids, so nothing ever reads it. End state: the run did not start, the log names the rule only as a failure, and the rule stays OFF for every user with no card or button on the Deploy page. This is the same ending QA findings 62/63 were fixed for, still open for the non-packaged path.
confirmed.why:
The claim survives; I found no guard.

- **Timeout becomes a plain refusal.** `background.js:4116-4118` (`sfFetch`) throws `Request timed out after 30 s` on abort, and `sfPatch` (`background.js:4578-4587`) has no handling for it. The message comes back as `{ error }`, so `_sftkWriteVerifiedCore` (`sftk-write.js:43-47`) returns `accepted: false` with the text `refused — Request timed out…`. An abort only cancels the client side; Salesforce can still commit the Tooling PATCH.
- **The rule is dropped from "maybe off".** `sftkVrPauseMaybeOff` (`sftk-vrpause.js:175-181`) reaches line 180 for a non-accepted result: `return !!r.pkg && /was submitted|may still finish/i.test(...)`. That is false for any non-packaged rule, and false for a timeout text even on a packaged one.
- **Nothing re-reads it.** `verifyAll` (`sftk-vrpause.js:199-200`) builds its id list only from `results[k].accepted`, and `sftkWriteVerifiedAll` (`sftk-write.js:113`) skips non-accepted results.
- **Nothing remembers or restores it.** In `sftkVrPauseOff` (`sftk-vrpause.js:228-249`), `touched = [...r.done, ...r.maybe]` excludes the rule. It gets no memory entry at line 230, no undo step at 233, and is not in the `sftkVrPauseOn(sess, touched)` call at 247.
- **The caller does not compensate.** `studio-deploy.js:2613-2619` only logs `pausedR.failed` and returns false. `afterWrites` and the `finally` both require `pausedR.ok`, and `_depRuleLeftovers` (`studio-deploy.js:2543-2544`) reads only the memory.

End state if Salesforce applied the PATCH: the run did not start, the log calls the rule "refused", and it stays off org-wide with no leftover card and no History undo step. The same holds for a dropped connection, or a 5xx whose resend throws.

It needs a metadata PATCH slower than 30 s or a connection lost after send, so it is rare, but the ending is the one findings 62/63 were fixed to prevent.
confirmed.fix:
In `sftkVrPauseMaybeOff` (`sftk-vrpause.js:180`), also count a non-accepted result whose outcome is unknown rather than a definite refusal, for any rule and not only packaged ones:

`return (!!r.pkg && /was submitted|may still finish/i.test(t)) || /timed out|Failed to fetch|NetworkError|network|HTTP 5\d\d|no answer/i.test(t);` with `t = String(x.text || '')`.

The rule then lands in `touched`: it is remembered, gets an undo step, and is switched back on when the run refuses to start. Switching on a rule that never went off is harmless, because the PATCH sends its own definition with `active: true`.

A stricter variant is to have `verifyAll` re-read `Active` for every rule rather than only accepted ids, and have `sftkVrPauseMaybeOff` treat a non-accepted rule as maybe-off unless that re-read shows it ON.

confirmed.title: Record editor Owner row promises the fallback queue on an object that queue does not take

- Insert: `background.js:2006` sets `nodeFallback = sftkOwnerFallbackFor(ownerFallback, qMap)`, and `background.js:106-110` returns null for a 00G id that is not in `qMap.takes`. - If it is a queue and `ownerCanQueue` is false, pass `''`.
- If it is a queue and `ownerCanQueue` is true, run one target query: `SELECT QueueId FROM QueueSobject WHERE SobjectType = '<obj>' AND QueueId = '<fallbackUserId>'` (the editor's owner search already runs this kind of query, per the claim). Keep the name only when a row comes back.
